correctness.rationale: For all integers p,q>=2 and B>0 the Laplacian is positive definite once any gain is positive; strict inverse-trace convexity makes the optimizer unique. The exact contrast-plus-2x2 block decomposition gives Phi(a,b); derivative at b=0 is strictly positive, and q^2 times derivative at a=0 equals F_{p,q}(B/pq). Strict convexity and the unique minimum of h_beta(t) prove every support phase. The exact p=2,q=6 cubic, the asymptotic c=sqrt(2) threshold and the two fixed-p budget laws follow by algebra. The standalone standard-library exact-rational checker passed 712 tests after reading actual files, including direct Laplacian inversion and gradients; finite checks support but do not prove all sizes.

originality.rationale: The precise all-budget support theorem for continuous diagonal gains on K_p join independent q and its sharp q ~ sqrt(2) p^(3/4) crossover were not covered by the inspected primary papers or published-finding corpus comparisons. Prior convex optimization principles, discrete/noise-free split-network selection and reentrant grounding on stars or K_{2,q} are explicitly acknowledged as related, not treated as the new result. The added clique edges change the matrix and thresholds, while the p->infinity threshold distinguishes the result from fixed-two-hub claims. Priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: A differently named preprint, thesis or unindexed table could give an equivalent complete split continuous-gain classification.
The related K_{2,q} and star results share a reentrant support mechanism; the genuinely additional structural claim is the general p,q phase inequality and sharp p^(3/4) crossover.
Finite verification does not itself establish scientific priority or independently validate the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural dense-core/periphery consensus network and the inverse-trace metric is a standard stationary-variance criterion. A complete necessary and sufficient support condition for all network sizes and budgets demonstrates genuine reentrant optimal actuation and identifies the smallest clique-two witness. The new, non-obvious 3/4-power imbalance threshold explains when this nonmonotone policy can occur as the core grows. Fixed-core budget windows span asymptotically separated 1/q and q^2 scales. The finding is a structural optimum and a sharp boundary rather than a one-off arithmetic example.
